newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Labour jumps 5 points in NZ Herald poll.
newsitem.headline: Labour jumps 5 points in NZ Herald poll.

text.p: Two weeks before a general election the main opposition Labour Party's support has jumped five points, a poll on Saturday showed.

The poll of 850 voters published in Auckland's daily newspaper, The New Zealand Herald, showed left-of-centre Labour with 21.8 percent support, up five points on a similar poll the week before and at its highest level in any poll since June.
The ruling conservative National Party was down 2.8 percent at 36.8 percent and the five party left wing grouping the Alliance shed three to 12 percent.
Economic nationalist New Zealand First was steady at 18.2 percent support.
A general election will be held on October 12.

If the poll figures were repeated on election night the three main opposition parties would have 69 seats in the 120 seat parliament -- easily enough to oust the National Party if they agreed to work together.
National's likely allies made little headway with free market ACT on 4.1 percent (four percent last week) and the morals-based Christian Coalition on 4.3 percent (four percent last week).

Under the mixed member proportional representation system adopted for the election, a party must score at least five percent support to win seats in parliament if it does not win one of the 65 constituency seats.

National's current coalition partner United scored 1.3 percent -- enough to qualify it for two seats in the House if, as seems likely, its Ohariu-Belmont candidate Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne wins his seat.
Translated into seats in the House, and presuming Dunne wins his seat, National would have 49 MPs, Labour 29, New Zealand First 24, the Alliance 16 and United two.
The poll was conducted by Waikato University by telephone in the week to September 25.
Thirteen percent of respondents were undecided how they would vote.

During the week the poll was taken former Labour leader Mike Moore accepted a long standing invitation to return to the Labour frontbench, healing a rift within the party; a rebel National group unsuccessfully asked its Wellington Central candidate to stand aside to give ACT a chance to win the seat; and the policies of the Christian Coalition aroused misgivings in National's liberal wing.

The average of the last three nationwide polls shows National with 38.1 percent support, Labour on 19.6 percent, NZ First 18.4, the Alliance 13.3, the Christian Coalition 4.6 percent and ACT 3.6 percent.
